CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient stepped off a curb while walking with his wife yesterday and landed on his left ankle incorrectly. He denies hearing or feeling a pop but describes the ankle as feeling stretched and extended. Pain is localized to the outside of the ankle and has been present for a couple of days. He was able to walk back to his house but with significant pain. Patient denies any previous substantial injuries to this ankle. Pain level is 8/10 without medication, improving to approximately 7/10 with ibuprofen. He has been treating with ibuprofen, elevation, ice, and weight-bearing precautions.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home and reports taking regular walks with his wife. He notes they have been taking walks frequently since working from home during COVID.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Stable with slight elevation, attributed to pain.
Left ankle: Ecchymosis and bruising over the lateral malleolus, swelling and edema present, tenderness to palpation on lateral side, soft tissue swelling noted. No joint laxity appreciated. No bony tenderness to palpation of foot.
Neurovascular examination of left foot: Capillary refill brisk, less than 3 seconds. Dorsalis pedis pulses strong. Motor and sensation intact. Findings symmetric bilaterally.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle: No fracture or bony abnormalities noted.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle pain - Ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex. The lateral ligament was stretched during the fall. Treatment plan: Continue RICE protocol (rest, ice, compression, elevation). Apply air cast for ankle stabilization. Prescribe crutches. Patient to stay off leg but begin walking as tolerated over the next several days. Continue NSAIDs to help reduce pain and swelling. Symptoms expected to improve significantly over 4-7 days. Follow-up visit in 2 weeks. Patient instructed to return if experiencing severe pain or other concerns requiring reevaluation.
